record.paper_title: Open Problems Related to Algebraic Attacks on Stream Ciphers
record.original_question: Let F_m:F_2^n→F_2^m be the augmented function associated with a stream cipher with linear transition L and Boolean filtering function f, defined by F_m(x) = (f(x), f(L(x)), …, f(L^{m-1}(x))). Find an algorithm that determines low-degree algebraic relations for this augmented function efficiently enough to support fast algebraic attacks when direct kernel computations become too large.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n,m\ge 1$ be integers and let $\mathbb{F}_2=\{0,1\}$ denote the binary field. Fix:
- a linear bijection $L:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{F}_2^n$ (the state-update map of a binary stream cipher whose internal state evolves by $x\mapsto L(x)$), and
- a Boolean function $f:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{F}_2$ (the filter).

Define the augmented function of length $m$
$$F_m:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{F}_2^m,\qquad F_m(x)=\bigl(f(x),\,f(L(x)),\,f(L^2(x)),\,\dots,\,f(L^{m-1}(x))\bigr).$$

An algebraic relation of degree $d$ for $F_m$ is a nonzero polynomial $R(X_1,\dots,X_n;Y_1,\dots,Y_m)\in\mathbb{F}_2[X,Y]/(X_i^2-X_i,Y_j^2-Y_j)$ of total degree at most $d$ in the variables $X_1,\dots,X_n$ (allowing arbitrary monomials in $Y_1,\dots,Y_m$) such that
$$R\bigl(x_1,\dots,x_n;\,F_m(x)_1,\dots,F_m(x)_m\bigr)=0\quad\text{for all }x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n.$$
Such relations are precisely the elements of the kernel of the evaluation map sending a polynomial $R$ to the vector $(R(x,F_m(x)))_{x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n}$, and they fuel fast algebraic attacks on the cipher.

Problem. Devise an algorithm that, given $L$, $f$, and parameters $m$ and $d$, determines a basis of (or at least produces nontrivial) algebraic relations of degree at most $d$ for the augmented function $F_m$, with running time and memory significantly better than that of directly computing the kernel of the full evaluation matrix (whose size grows as $2^n$ rows by $\binom{n}{\le d}\cdot 2^m$ columns), so that the procedure remains feasible in the regimes of $(n,m,d)$ relevant to fast algebraic attacks on real-world stream ciphers.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches surface follow-up work on algebraic immunity of augmented functions (e.g., analyses for Trivium) and on algorithms for finding low-degree annihilators/multiples of a single Boolean function, but no source identified provides a definitive efficient algorithm dedicated to computing low-degree relations for the augmented function $F_m$ that supersedes direct kernel computation. The status of this specific problem could not be conclusively verified from the search results.

status_evidence.title: Algebraic Attacks and Decomposition of Boolean Functions (Eurocrypt 2004)
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithms for deciding whether a Boolean function has low-degree multiples/annihilators, but for a single function f, not for the augmented function F_m.
status_evidence.claim: Related algorithms exist for single Boolean functions but not specifically as a complete answer for augmented functions.

status_evidence.title: Improving algebraic attacks on stream ciphers (eprint 2015/495)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses algebraic immunity of augmented functions and improvements to algebraic attacks; suggests Trivium has some immunity against algebraic attacks on augmented functions.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work studies algebraic immunity of augmented functions, indicating the problem remains an active research area without a settled efficient general algorithm.
